subject: SDK fallback behavior: canary + escape plan for BrightLane POC
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: SDK fallback behavior: canary + escape plan for BrightLane POC

Morning team —

Quick summary: BrightLane (POC, sandbox) is seeing occasional generation stalls when hitting long prefixes during demo traffic. They surfaced this over the weekend; Marissa and I paired with their engineer and captured a short repro. They want a short-term "escape/fallback" that keeps the demo stable this week and a follow-up roadmap ask for an SDK toggle or API parameter to opt out of aggressive prefetch/kv-cache merging.

Asks: 
- Logan: can platform confirm a minimal canary we can roll that forces the runtime to skip prefix prefetch for a route (low risk) and ship a temporary flag for BrightLane only?
- Marissa/Tessa: I need talking points for the customer (what we can do in the next 24h, and what is longer-term).
- Attachments: logs they sent (brightlane-request-logs.txt) and a draft canary plan (canary-rollout-plan-v1.pdf).

Why this matters: their execs are demoing this Friday. If we can't reduce the stalls they'll pause the POC. We should prefer a targeted canary over a global rollback.

Thanks —
Camila
Camila Reyes
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK fallback behavior: canary + escape plan for BrightLane POC

Thanks for the signal and the logs, Camila. I skimmed brightlane-request-logs.txt — looks like repeated KV cache prefetch attempts coincide with stall windows and a tokenization boundary that spikes memory usage. A few quick notes: 

- We can implement a route-level runtime toggle that disables prefix prefetch for a customer route; that is low risk and only a config change in routing/policies.
- I can draft a canary that targets their route ID with a 5% traffic bucket first, validate error/latency and then increase to 100% if stable.
- We should preserve the existing model variant (no model swap) to avoid quality regressions.

Roadmap ask: we should expose an opt-out flag in the SDK/server side as well, but that requires a small SDK change (a new header or client option) and a runtime check — estimate 2 sprints (engine + SDK owner).

I'll prepare the canary plan and a short rollback playbook by EOD. Two clarifying Qs: 
1) Which route ID are we targeting? (need the specific route/customer mapping for policy).
2) Do we have permission to apply customer-only config (BrightLane POC) without legal signoff? For short-lived POCs we typically proceed with engineering approval, but want to confirm.

- Logan
Principal Platform Engineer, Runtime

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Logan —
Thanks, that lines up. Quick answers: 
- Route ID: brightlane-sandbox-7 (mapped in HubSpot link).
- Legal: Marissa confirmed we can proceed with customer-specific policy changes for POC without additional signoff, as long as we document and revert after the demo.

Marissa — can you confirm the exec timeline so we can align the canary ramp plan?

Camila

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK fallback behavior: canary + escape plan for BrightLane POC

Confirmed — exec demo is Friday 2026-05-22 at 11:00 PT. They expect stable streaming during a 20m demo.

Customer ask summary for scripting: 
- Short-term: disable prefix prefetch for route brightlane-sandbox-7 for POC traffic (we prefer customer-only config).
- Medium-term: expose SDK switch or header so customers can toggle prefetch client-side for long prompts.

I also talked to our CS lead — if we can guarantee we will run the canary and revert after the demo we can continue to the next phase. Please add a one-line public-facing note I can send to Joe explaining the change and the rollback commitment.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK fallback behavior: canary + escape plan for BrightLane POC

All —

Canary plan attached and summarized below (see canary-rollout-plan-v1.pdf in attachments/drive):

- Step 0: Create route-level policy for brightlane-sandbox-7 that sets PREFETCH=false.
- Step 1: Roll the policy to 5% of traffic for 30 minutes; monitor 1m latency, 95th, and generation stalls.
- Step 2: If metrics stable, increase to 25% for 1h, then 100% for the demo window.
- Rollback: policy removed and route reverted within 15 minutes if errors increase >3x baseline or stalls reappear.

Public-facing line for Joe (1 sentence): "We will route your POC traffic through a temporary, customer-only setting that disables aggressive prefix prefetch to avoid stalls during the demo; we will revert this change after Friday's demo unless you request otherwise."

I'll schedule the canary to start tomorrow morning PST so we have a day to validate before the demo. Please reply-all with approval to proceed.

- Logan
Principal Platform Engineer, Runtime
